title_vi: Bốn kiểu hàng đợi trong chương trình: FIFO, bộ đệm vòng, ưu tiên, deque

claims.evidence: The Python collections (deque) and heapq documentation were read from a partial clone of python/cpython and the Disruptor technical paper from LMAX-Exchange/disruptor; all measurements come from the author's Python 3.13 runs on 2026-10-18 (the ring buffer is the author's own minimal implementation following the paper's slot and wrap rules).

mobile.evidence: Chromium (Playwright) rendered lesson.md (markdown-it, tables enabled, every <details> open, a 16 px page gutter) at each width: the page never scrolled sideways and the figure was scaled to the column; the smallest SVG font-size times that scale is the recorded minimum at 320 px. `python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser` measured every line of the figure in Chromium inside its box. Not GitHub, not a real phone and not learner testing.

claims.claim_vi: deque supports thread-safe appends and pops from either side with approximately O(1) performance, while list pop(0) and insert(0, v) incur O(n) memory movement; a bounded deque discards items from the opposite end when full, useful when only the most recent activity matters, like Unix tail.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of python/cpython at commit b00a14018172652226bd6efb517af021bd03aa88.

claims.claim_vi: heapq pops the smallest item; to keep equal priorities in insertion order, store (priority, entry count, task), the count acting as a tie-breaker.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of python/cpython at commit b00a14018172652226bd6efb517af021bd03aa88.

claims.claim_vi: The Disruptor's ring buffer is pre-allocated so entries are reused and create no garbage; a power-of-2 size lets a bit mask replace the remainder that maps a sequence to a slot; producers avoid wrapping the ring by tracking consumers' sequences.
claims.section: Design of the LMAX Disruptor: memory allocation, producers
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of LMAX-Exchange/disruptor at commit c871ca49826a6be7ada6957f6fbafcfecf7b1f87.

claims.claim_vi: Measured with Python 3.13: draining 100,000 items with list.pop(0) took 14.5 s and 14.0 s in two runs, with deque.popleft() 0.008 to 0.009 s; an 8-slot ring with an idle reader accepted 8 of e0..e9 and refused e8, then after 3 reads accepted three more with e10 in slot 2; deque(maxlen=3) after e0..e4 held e2, e3, e4; a heap of (severity, count, name) popped Binh, Dung, Chi, An.
claims.verified_by: The author ran and measured these on 2026-10-18 on one machine.

claims.claim_vi: The source states: Four queue types: simple FIFO, circular queue (ring buffer, with LMAX's low-latency ring buffer as an example), priority queue (heap), deque (supports FIFO and LIFO).

design_notes_vi: Bốn thẻ, mỗi thẻ một kiểu với kết quả chạy thử, và bốn câu hỏi để chọn. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: The source says a circular queue inserts at the front and deletes at the end; the lesson describes writer and reader moving the same way round the ring, as in the Disruptor paper.
The lesson adds the list.pop(0) cost, the two full-buffer policies (wait or drop oldest) and the tie-breaker for equal priorities.
